content.title: Where to watch the 2026 Masters Par 3 contest today on free streams, TV
content.text: Max Homa and his son, Cam Homa, walks on green on the seventh hole during par-3 contest at the Masters golf tournament, Wednesday, April 9, 2025, in Augusta, Ga. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Dustin Hockensmith | dhockensmith@pennlive.comThe 2026 Masters Par 3 Contest brings lighthearted golf ahead of a pressure-packed major that follows, with a Wednesday afternoon start at Augusta National Golf Club. Play is scheduled to start at noon ET with TV coverage on ESPN and streaming on-demand.How to watch the Masters Par 3 Contest on TV and stream without cable:When: Wednesday, April 8 at noon ETWhere: Augusta National Golf Club, Augusta, Ga.TV channel: ESPNStreaming on: FuboTV (free trial) | DirecTV (free trial) | SlingTV (low intro rate) | ESPN Unlimited ($29.99/mo.)Masters Par 3 Contest: Tournament at a glanceThe 2026 Masters Par 3 Contest will unofficially and lightheartedly kick off competition week at Augusta with nine holes of Par 3 golf with appearances from golfers’ family members and kids. Nicolas Echavarria carded a 5-under 22 and defeated J.J. Spaun on the second hole of a playoff to win the 2025 event, which featured a total of three holes-in-one along the way.The Masters’ official website describes the event: “Of all the traditions at the Masters, none is more endearing than the annual Par 3 Contest. This beloved event, held on Wednesday of Tournament week and now televised around the world, is above all a family affair. Wives and girlfriends, children and grandchildren, nieces and nephews-all happily serve as caddies. The sight of toddlers, outfitted in miniature Augusta National jumpsuits, toting a light bag or tending a flagstick more than twice their height brings smiles to onlookers near and far.”Masters Par 3 Contest: Know your live streamsFuboTV (free trial): FuboTV offers the most extensive package of live sports with rates competitive with DirecTV. The FuboTV Pro ($48.99 first month), Elite ($53.99) and Deluxe ($73.99) all come with first-month discounts. Monthly rates rise to $73.99, $83.99 and $103.99 after the first-month discount.DirecTV (free trial): DirecTV offers a 5-day free trial and a total of $30 off over the first three full months for the Choice Package, which includes 125-plus channels and access to ESPN Unlimited, a $29.99 standalone value featuring all ESPN channels and ESPN+.SlingTV (low intro rate): First full month of streaming runs as low as $29.99 with current offer for 50% off Sling’s Orange & Blue Plan. Day passes are also available for 24 hours ($4.99), as well as three-day ($9.99) and seven-day access ($14.99).ESPN Unlimited ($29.99 bundle): ESPN has a new, standalone package that includes ABC broadcasts, all of ESPN’s sports channels, and access to ESPN+. For a limited time, ESPN can be bundled with Disney Plus and Hulu for $29.99 per month.
